title: DET Reading & Vocabulary: Read and Complete, Read and Select & More
summary: The fast-fire reading and vocabulary tasks that make up much of the DET — and the pattern-spotting that wins them.

nodes.label: Read and Complete
nodes.note: Fill missing letters in words in a passage

nodes.label: Read and Select
nodes.note: Pick the REAL English words from a list

nodes.label: Fill in the Blanks
nodes.note: Complete a word with the right letters

nodes.label: Interactive Reading
nodes.note: A longer passage with several sub-questions

chunks.heading: Read and Complete — context fills the word
chunks.body: A short passage appears with **letters missing from many words**; you type the missing letters. The trick is **reading for meaning** — the sentence around each gap tells you the word, and English **spelling patterns** (common prefixes, suffixes, letter pairs) fill the rest.
chunks.realExample: 'The comp_ny ann__nced record pr_fits' → context + spelling give 'company announced profits'. Read the whole sentence before completing any single word.
chunks.memoryHook: Read for meaning first; spelling patterns finish the word. Context beats guessing letters.

chunks.heading: Read and Select — is it a real word?
chunks.body: You see a list of items and **select only the real English words** (the rest are invented non-words). It tests **vocabulary breadth** fast. Trust your instinct — if a word looks and sounds like real English you've seen, select it; if it's oddly spelled, skip it.
chunks.realExample: In a row like 'plausible / mordent / gribble / sincere', you'd pick 'plausible' and 'sincere' — and probably 'mordent' (a real music term) if you know it. Don't select convincing-looking fakes like 'gribble'.
chunks.memoryHook: Only tick words you genuinely recognise. A fake often has one letter that feels 'off'.

chunks.heading: Fill in the Blanks — spelling under time
chunks.body: You complete a **single word that has letters removed**, using the sentence for context. Same skill as Read and Complete but focused — quick reading plus accurate **spelling**.
chunks.realExample: 'She was ex_a_sted after the trip' → 'exhausted'. The meaning is obvious; the marks come from spelling it correctly and fast.
chunks.memoryHook: Meaning is easy; the points are in the spelling. Type it right, move on.

chunks.heading: Interactive Reading — the longer set
chunks.body: **Interactive Reading** gives a **longer passage broken into several tasks** — completing sentences, choosing the best title, picking the idea that fits, or highlighting the answer. Read the passage's **structure and main point** first, then answer each sub-task from the text.
chunks.realExample: If one sub-task asks for the best title, choose the option that covers the WHOLE passage, not just one paragraph — the classic trap is a title that's true but too narrow.
chunks.memoryHook: Get the passage's main point first; then every sub-task answers itself from the text.

recall.q: What do you do in the 'Read and Complete' task?
recall.a: Type the missing letters in words within a short passage, using context and English spelling patterns.

recall.q: What does 'Read and Select' test, and how do you approach it?
recall.a: Vocabulary breadth — you select only the real English words from a list and skip the invented non-words.

recall.q: Where do the marks mainly come from in 'Fill in the Blanks'?
recall.a: Accurate spelling — the meaning is usually easy, so correct, fast spelling earns the points.

recall.q: What does the 'Interactive Reading' task involve?
recall.a: A longer passage split into several sub-tasks (complete sentences, choose a title, highlight the answer) that you answer from the text.

recall.q: How should you choose the best title in Interactive Reading?
recall.a: Pick the option that covers the whole passage, not one that is true but too narrow.
